Subject: POC capacity planning - Acme AI

Hi Joe (and Sara),

Thanks again for the call today - great to meet the Acme AI team. Per our discussion, I wanted to summarize the proposed POC scope, success criteria, and an initial capacity plan so we can align on next steps and owners. I attached a lightweight POC template (poc_capacity_template.xlsx) you can edit.

High-level POC goals / success criteria:
- Functionality: Redwood inference integrated with Acme's inference client and serving production-like traffic patterns.
- Latency: 95th percentile generation latency <= 350ms for 512-token responses under target QPS.
- Cost: Token/unit cost within the test budget agreed during procurement (we can model after you share expected volume).
- Stability: No more than 0.5% error rate (timeouts / 5xx) during a 48-hour soak at sustained load.

Proposed evaluation plan / timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize POC scope and sign SOW (DocuSign link will follow).
- Week 1: Provision reserved capacity + basic integration (health checks, auth).
- Week 2: Run functional tests and short soak (24h).
- Week 3: Scale to target QPS and run 48h soak + regression checks.
- Week 4: Wrap-up call to review metrics and next steps (expand, contract, or production rollout).

Initial capacity suggestions (subject to your QPS/sequence profile):
- Reserved baseline: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated) for predictable throughput.
- Autoscaling: allow bursting to up to 16 GPUs for peak tests; use rapid warm-up pooling to reduce cold-starts.
- Burst expectations: 4x baseline -> 16x peak for short windows (minutes), with graceful queueing for sustained bursts.
- Caching: we recommend KV/prefix caching for repeated prompts which can reduce per-token cost and improve latency.

Open items for you to confirm:
1) Expected steady-state QPS and peak QPS (per model / route).
2) Typical sequence lengths (prompt + generation).
3) Any hard SLAs or security constraints (VPC, IP allowlists).

Next steps / owners:
- Marissa (me): finalize commercial terms and SOW; coordinate DocuSign.
- Vivek (cc'd): will provide technical sizing details and exact GPU + autoscaling configuration once you share QPS/profile.
- Monica (cc'd): will own CS onboarding and runbooks during the POC.

Please review and let me know the QPS/sequence details and any changes to the success criteria. Happy to set up a 30-min follow-up to lock capacity.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

Hi Joe / Marissa,

Thanks - great context. Based on the QPS and token profiles you shared, here's a recommended configuration and runbook notes for the POC.

Sizing summary (recommendation):
- Baseline reserved: 4x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs. This supports ~20-25 sustained QPS for generation (400-token outputs) when using Redwood continuous batching and KV caching.
- Autoscale ceiling: 16x GPUs for burst windows; this should absorb 70 QPS bursts with ~150-400ms additional queuing depending on batch alignment.
- Warm pool: keep 1 instance-per-GPU in a warm pool to reduce cold starts for short bursts; warm-up time from idle to usable is typically 20-45s for large models if the KV cache is cold.

Latency expectations (approx):
- Generation route (400 tokens) at steady-state (18 QPS): p95 ~ 280-340ms.
- Generation route during 70 QPS burst (with autoscale to 16 GPUs and warm pool): p95 ~ 380-650ms depending on cache hit rate and batch alignment.

KV / caching recommendations:
- Enable prefix caching for repeated prompts (saves ~30-60% of tokens in many evals).
- Persist KV cache between runs when possible for the 48h soak to improve tail latency.

Billing notes (POC):
- Reserved baseline GPUs billed at committed/dedicated rate per SOW.
- Burst (autoscale) usage above reserved baseline during the POC will be billed at the agreed on-demand add-on rate. We can include a capped burst credit for the POC if procurement requests it - Marissa can confirm commercial.

Operational runbook highlights:
- Health checks: 1m/10m agents for queue depth, p95 latency, and error rates.
- Fallbacks: configure automatic fallback to a smaller model variant if error rate crosses threshold to keep the integration live.
- Logging: enable token-level cost traces for first 48h so we can correlate cost vs QPS.

I attached a short spec sheet (redwood_poc_specs.pdf) with config knobs and exact instance types. Happy to jump on a quick 15-min call to walk through.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com
